question.problem:
Consider the matrix 
$B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}].$
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $B$ is upper triangular

II. $B$ is lower triangular

III. ${B}^{T}+B$ is upper triangular
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false, since $B$ has non-zero entries below the main diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement II is false, since $B$ has non-zero entries above the main diagonal:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & -2 & -4\end{aligned}]
$$

- Statement III is true, since the result of ${B}^{T}+B$ has all the entries below the main diagonal equal to zero:

$$
{B}^{T}+B=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
